propositions: Open/in_progress bugs with caused_by edges pointing to an epic or its descendants must deterministically block epic close, mirroring the direct-children gate with a teaching message (fix, re-parent, or dispute link).

Candidate bugs for relevance screening are filtered by deterministic criteria: status open or in_progress, type bug, and (created after the epic's first open→in_progress transition OR linked to the epic subtree any-relation any-depth, both directions), with a 32-candidate ceiling and overflow tally.

A single-turn haiku relevance screen uses model-class config and shared cache settings to force-choose A (deliverable-defect), B (pre-existing/adjacent), or C (unrelated) with one-line citation, running warm-then-fan-out; A-verdicts forward as compact candidates (title+citation+id, max 8 rows plus overflow) into the precheck-assembled fenced context.

The completion verifier blocks only an open defect-in-deliverable with no store-grounded disposition: either a supersedes/duplicates link (any direction, within subtree or to named successor) or reasoned pre-existence/deferral prose in the bug's description or comments; bare 'out of scope' and close_class do not qualify.

Screen output rides a registered epic_bug_screen_verdict schema with normalizing validator (overlap_verdict idiom); screen failure degrades open (logged) and never blocks; sidecar records full per-bug verdict tally including unevaluated-overflow count.
Commit-relation criterion was evaluated and rejected: 0 unique catches, 2 false positives, 58% of cited SHAs unresolvable (Gerrit rebase rot).
